sources.entry: Rust: _Add RISC-V Rust Operating System Tutorial_

summary.title: Stephen Marz: Blog (RISC-V Rust Operating System Tutorial)
summary.one_liner: A chapter-by-chapter tutorial for writing a small operating system for the RISC-V architecture in Rust, from setup and bootloading through memory, traps, processes, and filesystems.
takeaways: Set up a RISC-V development environment for Rust (Chapter 0), or skip to bootloading if you already have one.
Take control of the RISC-V hardware and build up communication over the serial console.
Implement page-grained memory allocation, a Memory Management Unit, and process memory.
Handle interrupts, traps, external interrupts, and system calls.
Build a block driver and filesystem so the OS can schedule user-space programs such as a shell, ls, and cd.
summary.summary: This is the index page for Stephen Marz's blog tutorial on writing an operating system for the RISC-V architecture in Rust. It lists 12 chapters, from setup and prerequisites through memory allocation, the MMU, interrupts and traps, process memory, system calls, starting a process, a block driver, filesystems, and userspace processes. The author notes that chapters 1 through 9 live in a chapters directory of the GitHub repo while chapters 10 and 11 are tags, and that the series is built up progressively. The stated goal is an OS that schedules user-space programs from a filesystem, including a shell, ls, and cd, as a demonstration of Rust for OS work.
